failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM654.920/921 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System Faults
items.whatHappens: The AdBlue dosing module or NOx sensors can fail, leading to warning lights, restricted performance (limp mode), and eventually a no-start condition if the tank is depleted and the system is locked out by the ECU.
items.repairVsReplace: Often resolved by replacing the dosing module or NOx sensor, which is a standard repair. If the tank heater or pump has failed, a full tank assembly replacement may be required.

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The internal matrix of the EGR cooler can crack, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases or enter the intake manifold. This leads to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock if severe.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard repair. If caught early, it prevents catastrophic internal engine damage.

items.title: Occasional Timing Chain Wear
items.whatHappens: While significantly improved over the OM651, some high-mileage OM654 units can exhibit timing chain stretch or guide wear, leading to a faint rattle on cold starts.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit replacement is straightforward. If ignored, it can lead to valve-to-piston contact, requiring a full engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM654 is generally considered a highly robust and reliable modern diesel. Units maintained with strict AdBlue top-ups and regular oil changes routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM654.920/921
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM654.920 and .921 are the primary 2.0L variants of the OM654 family. They are sometimes confused with the older OM651 or the larger OM656 inline-6. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM654 features a specific modular design, distinct AdBlue/SCR plumbing, and ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with an OM651 or OM656 without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM654.920/921 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM654.920/921 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof that the AdBlue system and EGR cooler are in good working order. Given the complexity of modern emissions systems, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM654 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by verifying the AdBlue dosing module, replacing the EGR cooler, and refreshing all critical seals, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM654 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage W213 E-Class or X253 GLC hosts where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM654 engine is installed by specialists familiar with modern Mercedes CDI systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM654 is typically found in W205, W213, and X253 vehicles valued between £8,000 and £30,000, a full replacement is generally financially viable and comfortably within the host vehicle's value . Replacement cost rarely exceeds the scrap threshold for these modern chassis, making a reconditioned unit a highly sensible investment.

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM654 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM654 engine typically costs between £3,000 and £5,000 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £3,520 to £5,780 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £1,800 but carry higher risk due to the complexity of the emissions systems. items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM654 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are AdBlue system faults, EGR cooler leaks, and occasional timing chain wear. AdBlue dosing module or NOx sensor failures trigger limp mode, while EGR cooler cracks can lead to unexplained coolant loss and white smoke from the exhaust.
